sections.h2: How quickly can a Pflugerville house be sold?
sections.html:
That depends on the route you take. A cash buyer may close within weeks, whereas a listing adds showings, an inspection and loan approval. Pflugerville is fifteen miles north of Austin on Farm Road 1825, and local buyers often measure it against Austin and nearby Round Rock.

Cash usually means a lower price in return for speed and a closing day of your choosing. A listing may net more but brings repairs, staging and a loan contingency. Compare both on paper.

  • Direct sale: best when a deadline, repairs, tenants or a lien get in the way.
  • Listing: best for a sound house and a patient seller.
  • Read each closing cost line before signing.

Pflugerville lies on Farm Road 1825 in northeastern Travis County. The Texas State Historical Association traces the name to Henry Pfluger, who arrived from Germany with his family in 1849; residents opened a school in 1872 and a Lutheran church in 1875.

A post office opened in 1893 under postmaster Louis Bohls. Around the mid-1890s about 250 people lived here and used Round Rock, eight miles northwest, for banking and shipping. After the Missouri, Kansas and Texas line ran just outside town in 1904, the population doubled to 500 within a decade.

People drifted to Austin after World War II, and by 1949 only 380 remained. Growth resumed in the 1960s, around the time of incorporation, and between 1980 and 1988 no Texas community grew faster. For a seller, the lesson is that houses here came in waves of new subdivisions, so builder and age tell a buyer more than the street does.

sections.h2: What else shaped Pflugerville before the suburban boom?
sections.html:
The handbook describes a small town with a weekly newspaper, the Press, published from 1907 to 1942. In the early 1920s several nearby school districts merged into the Pflugerville high school, which made the town a school center for the surrounding farms. A later weekly, the Pflag, began in 1980, just as the boom started.

The town's German farming roots survive in its name. The Pfluger family arrived in 1849, but the handbook says no real community formed at the site until after the Civil War, so the settlement is younger than the name suggests.

For a seller, local history is mostly color, but it supports one practical point. Older farmhouses and early town lots near the old center are a different product from tract homes built in the 1980s and after, and buyers price them differently. Say plainly which kind of house you have.

sections.h2: What does a Texas tax bill mean for a Pflugerville seller?
sections.html:
No state property tax exists in Texas, so the bill comes from local units like the county, school district and city. Value is set as of January 1 by the appraisal district, and that same day the year's tax lien attaches.

Bills go out near October 1. Whatever is unpaid on February 1 is late and draws a six percent penalty and one percent interest, with a possible collection fee of up to 20 percent. Homestead value notices arrive near April 1, and protests are generally due May 15.

  • Home you live in: $140,000 school exemption.
  • Age 65 or older, or disabled: an added $60,000 and a ceiling on school tax.
  • Cap: homestead appraisals may climb 10% a year at most.

Request a payoff from the Travis County tax office, and the title company will share this year's bill between seller and buyer.

sections.h2: Who records the deed for a Pflugerville sale?
sections.html:
Your deed is recorded by the clerk of the county containing the land, here the Travis County Clerk, after you sign it before a notary.

The clerk manual sets $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for every further page, with extra records fees. Your closing statement will show the total, and a warranty deed is typical.

Unsure of your parcel's county? Ask before the deed is drafted, because a deed filed in the wrong county slows closing.

sections.h2: What if the Pflugerville house has foreclosure or estate problems?
sections.html:
Every one of these runs on a short clock. A default notice gives you 20 days to pay the arrears and reinstate, and the sale notice must follow at least 21 days ahead of a first-Tuesday auction.

A lender whose sale falls short has two years to sue for the gap, and any surplus goes to junior lienholders, then to you. For an inherited house, a will is normally probated within four years of death, and an estate up to $75,000 not counting the homestead may use a small estate affidavit.

  • Behind on payments: get the reinstatement figure in writing.
  • Back taxes: ask the collector about an installment plan.
  • Inherited house: settle who may sign before accepting an offer.

sections.h2: What should I gather before showing a Pflugerville house?
sections.html:
Buyers in a fast-built suburb ask the same questions again and again, so answer them before they do. Start with the paperwork that proves what the house is and what has been done to it.

  • Your deed and survey, which show the legal description and any easements.
  • Permits and receipts for additions, roofs, air conditioning and fences.
  • The most recent tax bill and appraisal notice, plus any owners' association dues and rules.
  • Utility bills for a typical summer and winter month, since buyers from Austin will ask.

Then walk the property as an inspector would. Check the roof, the foundation line, the garage door, drainage around the slab and the water heater. Small foundation cracks and doors that stick draw attention, and a repair estimate in hand is better than a surprise at the inspection.

If you would rather not do any of that, a direct buyer will usually take it in present condition. Just make sure the written offer says so and that no repair requests can be added later without your agreement.

sections.h2: How should I compare offers on a Pflugerville house?
sections.html:
Judge each offer by what reaches your account and when. Deduct commissions, repairs, carrying costs, concessions and title charges from each price, then compare.

Ask if the buyer will close on your date, whether an inspection can end the deal, who buys the title policy and whether earnest money is required. If an owners' association covers the street, request its status letter early.

faqs.q: Which county records a Pflugerville deed?
faqs.a: Travis County, since the handbook places Pflugerville in northeastern Travis County. Ask the title company to confirm your parcel's county before the deed is drafted.

faqs.q: When did Pflugerville start growing quickly?
faqs.a: In the 1980s. The Handbook of Texas calls it the fastest-growing community in the state from 1980 through 1988, and its population reached 16,335 by 2000.

faqs.q: When are Pflugerville property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: After January 31. Interest and penalty start on February 1 under the Comptroller's calendar, and the penalty keeps rising monthly until July 1.

faqs.q: Is there a deadline to protest my Pflugerville appraisal?
faqs.a: Usually May 15, unless the notice arrives late and 30 days from delivery is later. Because the value dates from January 1, it also feeds into the year's tax split at closing.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Pflugerville house that is behind on the mortgage?
faqs.a: Yes. The loan is paid from your proceeds at closing. If a foreclosure notice has gone out, ask the servicer for the reinstatement amount and sale date, which falls on a first Tuesday.
